newsitem.title: CUBA: TENNIS-PERU COMES THROUGH DAVIS CUP TIE DESPITE MID-MATCH SHOWER.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-PERU COMES THROUGH DAVIS CUP TIE DESPITE MID-MATCH SHOWER.

text.p: Peru beat Cuba 3-2 in their Davis Cup American Zone group two first-round tie in Havana on the weekend despite losing one match after an unauthorised mid-match shower by Jaime Izaga.

In the first of Sunday's singles Juan Antonio Pino of Cuba brought the score level at 2-2, beating Izaga after referee Jaime Chavez gave the match to Pino because the Peruvian asked to go to the toilet but took the opportunity to take a shower.

Pino was ahead 1-0 in the third set, after losing the first set 4-6 and winning the second 7-5, when the referee stopped the match and awarded victory to the Cuban. His decision to give the match to Pino was approved by match supervisor Antonio Hernandez of the Domincan Republic.

Match officials told reporters that after Izaga's request to go to the toilet, Mexican match referee Jaime Chavez, seeing the Peruvian appeared to be taking some time, went to the bathroom area to check on what was causing the delay.
The officials said he saw that Izaga was taking a shower to refresh himself, although this is not allowed in the regulations.
Izaga appeared annoyed at the decision to stop the match. But the decision was not protested by Peru's captain, Jose Luis Noriega.
It then took a marathon four hours and 50 minutes for Peru's Americo Venero to beat Lazaro Navarro 7-6 6-3 6-7 2-6 8-6 and clinch the tie.
